requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Each obligation maps to at least one asserting test, and I found no requirement-violating behavior the reviewed tests would accept. I did not request implementation source.

**Mandatory inputs are recorded.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts the evidence `inputs` contain a requirements input for the subject, a definition input (`terms.readiness`), and outline inputs for `src/lib.rs`.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the mandatory test item `fn[ready_test]` and the definition input are recorded. It also runs `validate_repository` and asserts no evidence error for the accepted record, so the recorded formats pass ordinary evidence validation. It also asserts that an altered record is rejected.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` shows mandatory inputs carrying the subject, a cited requirement, and terms.

**Additional reads are recorded in the evidence input formats.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` covers item reads and line-range reads. It asserts recorded outline inputs equal `outline_input(...)`, which holds only file, selector and hash. It asserts recording is deduplicated and that nothing is recorded before `record_inputs`. It asserts failed reads and malformed request forms are errors. It asserts a read also records the terminology definitions.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` covers recording the innermost covering outline nodes, with no `text` or line numbers in the record. It covers plain-text `line@` nodes as well.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` covers the `requirements` and `definition` read forms. It asserts that `fresh.recorded_inputs()` equals the read's `input` plus its `definitions`, and that `read.inputs` equals the same list.
- In the CLI test, failed reads (`absent.txt`) and directory listings are not recorded, and repeated reads are recorded once.

**Selected search dependencies are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#fn[selected_dependencies_keep_the_delivered_hash_and_accumulate_without_reads]` covers selected tags producing an outline input with the delivered hash. It asserts a stale hash is detected by `validate_input`. It asserts accumulation across calls, harmless overlap with reads, and that an empty selection records nothing.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[a_helper_used_only_through_a_search_snippet_invalidates_saved_evidence_when_weakened]` asserts that a helper selected only through a search snippet appears as a hash-only outline input. It also asserts that weakening the helper invalidates the evidence, and that unrelated items are not recorded.

**Only supplied sources are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` asserts each page's inputs equal that page's own inputs plus definitions.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded]` asserts that only inputs from pages actually delivered to the model end up in the evidence, and that undelivered entries do not.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` asserts that `references` discovery records nothing. It asserts the unread `fn[ready]` is recorded only after the read, and recorded once.

**The harness creates the records itself.** The tests build evidence only through harness paths such as `record_inputs` and the finish and read dispatch. They assert the result equals `outline_input(...)` and that the ordinary validators accept or reject it.

The text of the cited formats (`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`, `requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, `requirements.definitions.inputs`) is context. Their own validation is not reassessed here.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each tag selected by a valid `finish_search` call, the harness MUST record
its `file`, `item`, and structural hash as an outline input under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` before acknowledging that call.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
